prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1499; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.

Q: Understood. Let's start with where you were when the collision happened.

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward the highway on-ramp. It was late afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what was the other vehicle doing?

A: I was going straight. The other car came across into my lane. I think they were trying to pass a slow truck, but I can't say for certain.

Q: How fast were you going when you noticed the other vehicle?

A: Maybe twenty-five miles an hour, maybe less. I was braking when we hit. It wasn't a hard hit, more like a bump that stopped us both.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. My car just jolted forward and back.

Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness at any point?

A: No, I didn't hit my head. I stayed awake the whole time and got out of the car on my own.

Q: Where do you feel pain or discomfort now?

A: My neck is stiff and sore, and my lower back aches, mostly when I sit for a long time or get up from the couch. I started noticing it the next morning.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that evening and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since. The doctor said it was a strain.

Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this accident?

A: Not that I can recall. I had a little stiffness after my workouts sometimes, but nothing that stopped me from doing anything.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just hope I can get back to normal soon.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
